main_text.l: ualla[?],siue in tres regiones apte distinguitur.
Prima est suprema,eademq; purior,necnon sub-
tiliori referta aere,atq; calidior. In hac autem pro-
ducuntur plurimum meteora ignea:ut cometæ,ful-
mina,&c.
Secunda,infima,nobis uicina, denso ac crassiore
aere referta, in qua gignuntur μετέωρα aquea : ut
nubes,pluuiæ, atq; æstate ros,hyeme pruina: ille ui
caloris,hæc uero frigoris.
Tertia,media inter has duas constituitur,eadeq;
mixto aere referta: in qua locum iudicantur habe-
re nix,grando,& aerea quædam meteora. Quam-
uis hanc tertiam regionem Aristoteles in præsenti
capite non prorsus ita distinguit: ufurpata tamen
hæc est partitio omnibus recentioribus, ac sumpta
quidem ex ijs quæ ab Aristotele explicantur lib. 1.
Meteororum, cap.11.ac 12.ubi de grandine agit ex
sententia Anaxagoræ.
Quæ est natura aeris,siue uniuersi eius
spacij quod inter orbes cœlestes
ac terram interponitur?
Hanc quæstionem mouet Aristoteles occasione
quæstionis præcedētis.Fuit autem de ea quæstione hæc
quorundā ueterū opinio:Arbitrati sunt cœlū ipsum
unà cū stellis naturæ esse igneæ, ideoq; toto illo or-
bium cœlestiū interuallo elementum ignis contine-
ri:spacium autē inde ad nos usq; uniuersum solo im-

page.notes: The first word of the page, "ualla", is not certain; I read it as a fragment and marked it [?]. The Greek word μετέωρα is copied as I see it, and the accents are uncertain. The chapter numbers in "cap.11.ac 12." are read from the scan and are not certain. The page number "295" is set in an old form and is read as 295. The sentence ends with the printed hyphen of "im-" and continues on the next page; the catchword "pleri" is recorded at the foot.
